author: Henry Ketcham
claims: There were not less than three known attempts on the life of Lincoln between Springfield and Washington.
Lincoln was accustomed to riding alone to and from the Soldier's Home.
Lincoln's friends were in daily fear of kidnapping or murder.
Lincoln believed he would live to complete his specific work and not live beyond that.
Lincoln's trustfulness must have disarmed some.
The wonder is not that he was slain at last, but that under the circumstances he was not slain earlier.
Had he heeded the last caution of his devoted friend, he would not have been shot in 1865.
